---
indicator_code: "TAT-001"
indicator_name: "Claims Turnaround Time (TAT)"
definition: |
  The **number of days elapsed between claim creation and payment confirmation** in the
  ERP. TAT measures the speed of the claims settlement pipeline and is used to monitor
  operational efficiency and compliance with payment timelines.

  Three summary statistics are tracked: **minimum**, **median**, and **maximum** TAT,
  along with the share of claims settled within **30 days**, **90 days**, and **after
  90 days**.
numerator: |
  For each paid claim:

  > **TAT (days) = Date Paid − Date Created**

  - **Date Created** — timestamp the claim was first entered into the Payor system
  - **Date Paid** — date payment was confirmed in the ERP
denominator: |
  Total number of **paid claims** in the selected period (used for median/mean
  calculations and percentage-based KPIs).
unit_of_measure: "**Days** (whole numbers; floor, not rounded)."
data_source: |
  - **ERP** — payment date
  - **Payor System** — claim creation date

frequency: "Monthly aggregation; trend charts show month-over-month movement."
disaggregation: |
  - Fund Scheme (SHIF/ECCIF/POMSF/PHC)
  - County
  - Facility Level (Level 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / National Referral)
  - Facility
sdg_who_ref: |
  **SDG 3.8** — Universal Health Coverage; timely provider reimbursement is a
  prerequisite for sustained service delivery.
notes_caveats: |
  - Only **paid claims** are included
  - Outliers (very high TAT values) can inflate the **maximum TAT** metric — use
    **median TAT** as the primary operational benchmark.
  - TAT is calculated from the **creation date**, not the submission or approval date,
    so it captures the full end-to-end pipeline.
  - County-level figures reflect claims processed by facilities within that county,
    not necessarily patients residing there.
---
